items.title: The World Is Yours
items.summary: The 32-year-old rapper made his name with audacious punchlines and moments of startling candor, but his latest album is weighed down by a pervasive air of exhaustion.

items.title: Honest Feeling Album (素直な気持ちアルバム)
items.summary: The omnivorous Japanese producer’s new LP jams a little of almost everything: knotty freeform jazz, proggy pop, noisy electronics, and triumphant J-rock.

items.title: Heavy Blessings: A Church Road Records Primer
items.summary: How the sudden demise of Holy Roar Records kickstarted one of the most venerable indie labels in the UK. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Haruomi Hosono, “Yours Sincerely”
items.summary: The latest from the Japanese icon functions as a showpiece for his many musical eras. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Ow ∞
items.summary: The world has finally caught up with the North Carolina alt-pop duo, whose playful and unsettled fifth album speaks to its moment with newfound lucidity.

items.title: Brighter Blue EP
items.summary: On her latest covers EP, the singer-songwriter offers refreshing, timely interpretations of blues and gospel classics.

items.title: Synthetic Water Music
items.summary: Following a 2023 compilation dedicated to birdsong, the Slovak label Mappa turns its focus to aquascapes both real and imagined, spanning decades of field recordings and ambient experiments.

items.title: Gao Dan Dan EP
items.summary: The Danish Chinese musician (and Zara Larsson collaborator) concentrates her multi-cultural cool into a collection of bilingual club bangers and sparkling alt-pop gems.

items.title: In Visible Silence
items.summary: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the second album from a mischievous group of provocateurs whose high-tech hijinks anticipated a sea change in pop, dance, and hip-hop.

items.title: Dog on the Rock / Seven Off the Two / Seaplane Dog / The View from Tian Tan
items.summary: Originally issued as tour-only CD-Rs, these four diaristic albums from the singer-songwriter bundle together half-formed suites of slow, seasick recordings aimed squarely at the die-hards.

items.title: It’s Not Easy Being Greenland
items.summary: The country is simultaneously well-known and woefully overlooked. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Angela Autumn, “Believer”
items.summary: Embracing everything from psych-rock to indie folk, "Rose of Appalachia" breaks out of the old-time music box. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Essential Releases, September 11, 2026
items.summary: Glitch pop, old time music, hip-hop, and more. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Sylvan Esso Pick Their Bandcamp Favorites
items.summary: On the event of their latest LP, we asked Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn to pick some recent faves. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: The Singer in My Band
items.summary: On his first album for Matador, Nate Amos trades the magpie charm of his past solo work for a warm, twangy, and tightly constructed approach. It’s the sound of a songwriter sketching out his own gospel.

items.title: Distance in Static
items.summary: On what he has hinted may be his final “traditional” LP as Bonobo, the UK producer cycles through moods and styles, with a particular focus on the clubby soundscapes of his DJ era.

items.title: Slime Language 3
items.summary: The gargantuan third installment of Young Thug’s label compilation series inducts a new class of YSL and ØWay acolytes to the collective’s post-RICO reconstruction. It’s a rich and unwieldy text.

items.title: Nine
items.summary: The instrumental trio spends its ninth album almost entirely in attack mode, pulling from death metal and hardcore for one of its heaviest and most riff-forward releases to date.

items.title: Solex Does It Again
items.summary: Revisiting the quirky joys of Elisabeth Esselink's '90s cut-and-paste indie project. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Kristin Hersh Comes Home
items.summary: The Throwing Muses co-founder reflects on her deeply personal new album and the people who inspired it. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Nate Mercereau, “Fantastic Thoughts”
items.summary: L.A. post-jazz instrumentalist and Andre 3000 collaborator pivots to radiant prog fantasia. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: B’DAY (20th ANNIVERSARY EDITION)
items.summary: With independent spirit and fresh inspiration from New York rap, Beyoncé’s 2006 solo album was a creative breakthrough, but this prestige reissue does little to contextualize its pivotal moment in her career.

items.title: Miraggi
items.summary: Inspired by the riches of the Tuscan coast, producer David August and percussionist Lorenzo Setti concoct a pitch-perfect nirvana of Mediterranean chill-out music.

items.title: Bad Bunch
items.summary: On her band’s first LP in 12 years, Royal Trux’s Jennifer Herrema trades the vintage hard rock of previous albums for a woozy mix of hip-hop, R&B, dub, and pawn-shop electronics.

items.title: femme fatale
items.summary: The UK-born rapper’s second album of the year is busy but breezy, a well-calibrated mix of rage textures and mellower grooves with Caribbean and Afrobeats influences.

items.title: The Best New Electronic Music on Bandcamp, August 2026
items.summary: Our guide to the month’s crucial electronic LPs. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Jem Finer and John Matthias on the Strange Magic of “Almost Starlight”
items.summary: Two decades of friendship culminate in a spectral album of violin and hurdy-gurdy recorded inside an ancient English church. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Vanishing Twin, “Archives”
items.summary: Yé-yé grooves collide with images of life and art in a gleaming Space-Age future on the London act's latest. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Cicada Hum: No-Neck Blues Band Returns
items.summary: Like a troupe of no-wave hippies, the New York group sowed chaos while inspiring much creativity. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: doseone, Wino Willy & Zetroc, “sighting”
items.summary: A horror film made without a single frame of celluloid. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .

items.title: Brazil’s New Metal Vanguard
items.summary: Brazil's heavy metal scene finds itself on unusually open ground. Read full story on the Bandcamp Daily .
